idiom: hit the nail on the head
meaning: to describe or identify exactly what is causing a situation or problem
example: Your comment really hit the nail on the head: the budget was the real problem.
origin: Comes from carpentry, where a carefully aimed hammer blow drives the nail straight into the wood

wrong_meanings.meaning: to fail badly at a practical task
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is about accuracy in identifying something, not about failing at a task

wrong_meanings.meaning: to repeat the same argument again and again
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: Repetition is not implied; the idiom describes getting to the exact point in one go

wrong_meanings.meaning: to work slowly and very carefully with tools
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes the physical activity literally, not the figurative meaning of precision in speech or thought

explanation: 'Hit the nail on the head' comes from carpentry and means saying or identifying exactly the right point. Ukrainian speakers may try to translate it word for word, so learn it as a whole unit meaning 'to state the core of the matter precisely'.
